title: The Prolouge
author: Salaknib
body:
There are many ways to fight. Physically and mentally.


Each with their weapons.

A bullet leaves a hole. A knife leaves a scar.

The mind is different.


A commander uses propaganda.

A politician uses fear.

A parent can use guilt.

A lover can use silence.

A friend can betray trust.

A person can gaslight themselves.


Isn't it funny? The most deadly of weapons? Not guns or blades, but the one everyone has.

You can wound a man without ever touching him.

You want to know what they are?

Weapons that make a man doubt what he knows. _Seeds._

Weapons that make a man obey. _Chains._

Weapons that sever a man from everyone around him. _Knives._

Weapons that turn a man's own emotions against him. _Fire._

Weapons that bury the person underneath the wounds. _Graves._


**Doubt.**

A man who knows his enemy can fight him.
A man who does not know whether his enemy exists cannot.


**Gaslighting.**

Sow the seed.
Tell him what he saw did not happen.
Tell him what he remembers is wrong.
Tell him everyone else remembers differently.
Do it long enough, and eventually he will stop asking whether you are lying.
He will ask whether he is sane. If he is still him.


**Propaganda.**

Do not tell a man what to think.
Tell him what everyone else thinks.
Give him a thousand voices repeating the same thing, and soon his own voice will sound like the strange one.
For a voice in a cacophony of voices is nothing but noises.


**Contradiction.**

Tell him one truth.
Then another.
Then take the first away.
Keep changing the ground beneath his feet.
Eventually, he will stop looking for solid ground.


The wounds...are a place where these seeds will go.
That is where the stem that has the thorns will grow.
Doubt makes a man uncertain.
But for them to move?


**Fear.**

A useful weapon.
It does not need to be real.
It only needs to feel real.
A shadow behind a door.
A letter without a name.
A threat without a date.
Sometimes the greatest weapon is not knowing when it will come.


**Guilt.**

A quieter chain.
Make a man believe that his suffering is his fault.
Then make him believe that obedience is the only way to make things right.
He will put the chains on himself.


**Obligation.**

Tell him what you have done for him.
Remind him what he owes you.
Keep a debt alive long after it has been repaid.
Some men will endure anything rather than be called ungrateful.


**Reverse Psychology.**
Tell a man not to do something.

Make him believe the choice is his.
The cleverest cage is the one the prisoner mistakes for freedom.


_The Chains_ of Submission.

A man does not need to be forced if he can be convinced to volunteer.

But you know what makes one so deadly?


A lonely man is easier to break.

Not out of weakness no.
Because there is no one left to tell him that he is being broken.


**Isolation.**

Remove the family.
Remove the friends.
Remove the people who knew him before.
Then become the only voice remaining.


**Silence.**

The absence of an answer can be more cruel than an answer itself.
Tell a man something terrible is coming.
Then say nothing.
He will imagine a thousand endings.
Most will be worse than the truth.
That is the beauty of silence.
The enemy does not have to create the fear.
The victim creates it for him.


**Betrayal.**

Trust is a door.
Betrayal is teaching a man that opening it was a mistake.
Do it once, and he becomes cautious.
Do it enough times, and he stops opening doors altogether.


**Rejection.**

Make a man believe that he is unwanted.
Eventually, he will begin removing himself from places where nobody asked him to leave.


Loneliness is the scars, the bleeding wounds, these ones make

And loneliness makes excellent soil.


Fear is obvious.

There are worse things. And how blinding they are. For it is what everyone seeks, like flies to shit.


**Hope.**

Oh. Beautiful Hope...

Give a man light.

Give him something to live for.

Give him a reason to endure the flaying, the scars.

Then take it away.

Fear tells a man that tomorrow will be terrible.

Hope tells him that tomorrow might be beautiful.

That is why hope can be crueler.

A man will endure almost anything if he believes the suffering will end.


**Love.**

The nectar of gods and monsters.

The stronger the attachment, the deeper the wound.

You do not need to hurt the man.

Hurt what he loves.

He will do the rest himself trying to save them. trying to cover them.

"My love! Oh, my love! I will be your shield!"

And watch them dissolve into a *sobbing.* **broken.** ***mess.*** as they hold their corpse.


**Grief.**

Grief is a fire that feeds on memory. That feeds on the seeds, the chains, the knives.

You cannot always extinguish it.

Sometimes all you can do is teach a man to carry it.

And carry it they shall. for they will take it in like a orphaned child.


**Shame.**

Make him believe that what he did is not merely something he regrets.

Make him believe it is what he is.
There is a difference between:

*“I did something terrible.”*

And:

*“I am terrible.”*

The first can be forgiven. The second can become a prison.

Desperation. That is the burns the Fires leave.

A desperate man will destroy himself just to reach the thing he believes will save him.

And what is the man beneath all of this? 

Where is a corpse buried when they are nothing more but a husk of their former self?

_Graves_. They leave nothing recognizable behind.


**Memory.**

A man's memories are his evidence. His precious, so so precious proofs.

Proof that he lived.

Proof that he loved.

Proof that he suffered.

Take those away, and what remains?


**Identity.**

Tell him what he is often enough, and eventually he may stop deciding for himself.

Soldier.

Coward.

Monster.

Hero.

Traitor.

Parent.

Murderer.

Names are strange things.

Put one on a man long enough, and he may begin wearing it like a uniform.


**Purpose.**

A soldier can survive terrible things if he believes they mean something.

Take away the meaning.

The scars of suffering remains.


**Trust.**

Once all is said and done, once the mind has been broken and the truth finally revealed...

shatter the trust as well.

Not merely trust in others.
Trust in himself.

Make him wonder whether every kindness was a trap.

Every memory, false.

Every friend, an enemy.

Every decision, a mistake.

That is when a man becomes truly alone.

Dissolution is what Graves are.


The death of the person who was there before.

No blood. No funeral. No grave.

Just absence and the hole where they once were.


There is one weapon that does not belong to any category.

It's not the strongest. but it's the second best.

a jack of all trades.


**The Lie**

A lie can create doubt.

A lie can create fear.

A lie can destroy trust.

A lie can isolate.

A lie can create hope

A lie can destroy hope.

A lie can change a man's memory.

A lie can change his identity.


And the greatest lie of all?

That the war is over.

I... 
used to think war was fought with guns.
Then I thought it was fought with men.

Wrong. oh how wrong I am.

War is fought with whatever a man can use to make another man surrender.

Sometimes a rifle.
Others are word, 
and a handful is silence.

But...

Sometimes the enemy does not have to do anything at all.
Sometimes all he has to do is leave the door open.

And wait for you to walk through it.
That is the thing nobody tells you about war.

The battlefield does not always follow you home.

you bring it with you. Willing or not.
